operator_io_quirks: Backtick-quoted DDL identifiers (`Investors`, `Investor_details`); mixed case table/column names; must re-quote with " in generated SQL.
Tiny DB (all tables <=20 rows); read_schema sampling trivial, no huge-table path exercised.
date_of_transaction declared DATETIME but storage class text with 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS' values; ts_fuzzer dispatch: contains 'date' -> first element parses as int? no -> Date fuzzer.
amount_of_transaction DECIMAL(19,4): number family, scale=19 precision=4 -> Number(scale=19); storage mixed real/integer; values up to ~3e5.
share_count VARCHAR(40) but values are numeric strings ('8718572','9'); String fuzzer, int-like strings get +-1 neighbours.
other_details VARCHAR(255) 100% NULL, distinct 0, no samples -> String sampler with empty elements -> p:=1, all fresh random strings.
Purchases and Transactions_Lots have NO primary key (pk=[]); sample_fresh_primary_keys must no-op; drop_unique_duplicates no-op.
Sales.sales_transaction_id is PK AND FK to Transactions.transaction_id (1:1 child); FK drawn from parent's final values then PK dedup.
Purchases.purchase_transaction_id NOT NULL FK, no PK -> duplicates allowed, no dedup; NOT NULL not enforced in Python, insert failures skipped.
Ref_Transaction_Types has only 2 rows ('PUR','SALE'); FK children draw from 2 values -> heavy ties in transaction_type_code.
Investors.investor_id PK 20 rows, Lots.investor_id FK distinct 9 (subset); Transactions.investor_id distinct 10; FK fan-out uneven.
All FKs resolve to existing parents; no dangling/self FKs; no composite keys; no CHECK/UNIQUE column constraints beyond PKs.
operator_ts_expectations: Date fuzzer on date_of_transaction: template from first parsable element, likely '%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S'; range from min/max parsed dates (~1977..2001); fresh dates uniform in that range.

Number fuzzer on amount_of_transaction: scale=19 -> range [-1e19,1e19], list_max overwritten to full max; fresh draws wildly larger than original ~3e5 -> implausible amounts (FN risk on SUM/AVG thresholds).
Number fuzzer on integer PKs/FKs: +-1/+-2 perturbation of elements; PK dedup keeps first occurrence; small tables -> many collisions, few surviving rows.

String fuzzer on transaction_type_code: elements 'PUR','SALE' plus pool literals; fresh random strings over a-zA-Z0-9() length 0..10 -> FK values not matching Ref table unless drawn from parent (they are, via fill_foreign_keys_consistently).
String fuzzer on share_count: int-like strings get str(i+1),str(i-1); contaminate 50% -> numeric comparisons on share_count may see non-numeric strings (FP/FN).
other_details all-NULL original: elements empty -> p:=1 -> all fresh random strings; queries filtering other_details IS NULL will find none (FN).
Ref_Transaction_Types only 2 rows: choose_table_sizes may give it 1..2500 rows; FK children draw with replacement from 2 values -> extreme ties; DISTINCT/GROUP BY counts implausible.
Purchases/Transactions_Lots no PK: no dedup, rows can repeat exactly; COUNT(*) inflated vs original 15.
Sales 1:1 with Transactions in original; TS draws sales_transaction_id from Transactions values with replacement then PK-dedups -> still 1:1-ish but may miss some transactions (FN on anti-join).
Small original sizes (15-20) vs TS sizes 1..2500: cardinality-based queries (COUNT comparisons) likely FP/FN.
Date fuzzer p-inversion: p=0.2 means element returned 20% of time, 80% fresh uniform dates -> dates spread over 24 years, not clustered like original.
No CHECK/UNIQUE/NOT NULL enforcement in Python: NOT NULL FK columns may get NULL if parent empty (not here) or insert-fail rows skipped -> row counts below target.
